newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indian Sep diesel purchases seen at low levels.
newsitem.headline: Indian Sep diesel purchases seen at low levels.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) is expected to limit its high speed diesel purchases in a tender for September to under 300,000 tonnes, traders said on Friday.
"It will not be stunning," one trader said.
Some said IOC might even take less than 200,000 tonnes, in line with the 165,000 tonnes it bought for August delivery, due to a low demand month amid the monsoon season.
IOC took only six to seven cargoes of diesel in September last year.
The tender closed on July 31 and would be awarded this evening.

The frontrunner in the tender is a major European oil company with its offers to the Indian east coast for both the 1.0 and 0.5 percent sulphur grade at around 47-50 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis.

The major's offers to the Indian west coast are around 20 cents per barrel discount to Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f basis, which is equivalent to just over $1.00 per barrel premium to MidEast spot quotes.
Other low offers were made by another European major at around $1.80 per barrel premium to MidEast spot quotes, c-and-f east coast, and just over $1.00 premium to MidEast quotes, c-and-f west coast.
A western and a Japanese trader also made low offers.
Most offers to the east coast were more than $2.00 premium to MidEast spot quotes, c-and-f west coast.
In its tender for August, IOC awarded east coast cargoes at $1.75 per barrel above MidEast spot quotes for the 1.0-percent grade, and at 35 and 50 cents above Singapore quotes, c-and-f basis.
A west coast cargo of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel was awarded at a 52-cent discount to Singapore quotes, c-and-f basis.
